About the job  The opportunity     We are building the AI for home life. Just Move In helps people set up and run their home. Our AI agent Jay handles energy, broadband, water, insurance and council tax when someone moves, and we are evolving into a full Home OS for everything that comes after.     Here's the thing: we don't win users through marketing. We're embedded in the systems that already know someone is moving (letting agents, CRM platforms, deposit schemes, property portals). That's our distribution moat, and it will deliver 1M UK moves a year by 2028.     The role     We're hiring a full stack Product Engineer     Engineer first: you'll ship real code across Jay and our core platform every week. But with a product mindset: you get a problem and a metric, not a spec, and you work out the rest. Talk to users, look at the data, decide what to build, build it, watch what happens. You think in systems and how to architect for both user experience and scalability.     We're a small, senior, AI-native team. Your decisions ship.     What you'll do     • Ship product end to end. Take a problem like ""movers drop off between quote and purchase"" from investigation through to shipped, measured code, across Jay (Python, FastAPI, pydantic-ai) and our Laravel 11 core.  • Build the agentic product. Jay is how movers experience us: tool-calling, LLM workflows, evals. You'll make it smarter and more reliable with every release.  • Own outcomes, not tickets. Work directly with design, commercial and the founders. Prototype fast, ship the simplest version, iterate on what the data says.  • Work AI-native. AI coding agents (we run Claude Code) are a core part of your workflow, and you'll help shape Alan, our in-house AI engineer.  • Keep the quality bar where it matters. This is code real revenue depends on: tests (Pest, PHPUnit), sensible observability, careful handling of customer data.     Your first 90 days     • Understand the product deeply: where movers come from, where they drop off, what partners need.  • Ship something that measurably moves a number. Small is fine, shipped is the point.  • Establish your rhythm with design, engineering and commercial. You're a peer to all three.     You might be right if     • You have 3-7 years of engineering experience with strong backend foundations in PHP/Laravel or Python, and enough range to work across the stack (we run Next.js, Nuxt and Vue on the frontend).  • You've shipped things users touched, and you cared what happened next. You watched the metric, learned, and iterated.  • You're comfortable in ambiguity. Given an outcome and a why, you can find the path without a spec or a big team.  • You ship fast. You'd rather ship something imperfect and learn than debate the perfect solution.  • You're commercially minded. You understand which work moves revenue and which is just interesting.  • You communicate clearly with engineers, designers and commercial people alike.  • You've been through a scaleup. You've watched a product and team grow fast, and you kept shipping through the mess.  • You love to build. Side projects, weekend prototypes, tools you made because you wanted them to exist. We'll ask to see them.     AI-native is non-negotiable     You already use AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor or similar) daily. Not as an experiment, as your workflow. You spec with AI, prototype with AI, analyse with AI, and review the output with strong technical judgment. In your application, tell us how AI has changed the way you build. Be specific.     Bonus points     • You've shipped production AI, agentic or LLM systems: RAG, agents, tool-calling or evals (pydantic-ai a plus).  • You're comfortable in both Python and PHP.  • You've built partner or API integrations: webhooks, data pipelines, messy third-party data made reliable.     You're probably not right if     • You need a spec and a ticket before you can start.  • You only want to write code. Talking to users and digging into data feels like someone else's job.  • You optimise for consensus over velocity. We move fast, disagree openly, and commit fully.     Our stack     Laravel 11 (PHP), Aurora MySQL, Redis, Horizon, Pest and PHPUnit. Jay runs on Python, FastAPI and pydantic-ai. Next.js 15, Nuxt 3 and Vue on the frontend. AWS (London), Datadog, Sentry, GitHub Actions. Claude Code and Alan, our in-house AI engineer, woven through how we build.     How we work     • Empowered teams: we give you problems to solve, not features to build.  • AI-native: our codebase is designed for agents, and our thinking starts with ""what would this look like if AI did it?""  • Velocity obsessed: we bias toward shipping, learning and iterating.  • High standards with psychological safety: direct feedback, blameless incidents, room to take risks.  • A clear, published career framework: you'd join at mid or senior level with a transparent path onward.     The details     • Competitive salary + meaningful equity.  • Hybrid in London.  • You'll work alongside a team who have worked at Uber, Apple, Match Group, Microsoft, Google and Meta.  • Just Move In is a certified B Corp. We particularly welcome applications from women and underrepresented groups in technology, and we're happy to make adjustments to the interview process.     Interested?     We're not looking for a CV-perfect candidate. We're looking for someone who reads this and thinks ""this is exactly the problem I want to solve.""     Apply with your CV and a short note: what excites you about building the AI for home life, how AI has changed the way you work, and what you'd ship first. JobTitle: Senior Software Engineer — Anywhere Cloud Cloudera Object Store
JobDescription: About the job  Business Area:   Engineering  Seniority Level:  Mid-Senior level  Job Description:  At Cloudera, we empower people to transform complex data into clear and actionable insights. With as much data under management as the hyperscalers, we're the preferred data partner for the top companies in almost every industry. Powered by the relentless innovation of the open source community, Cloudera advances digital transformation for the world’s largest enterprises.  What You'll Build  Cloudera is reimagining object storage for the Kubernetes era. You will contribute to the design and implementation of AWC (Anywhere Cloud), our control plane for running data infrastructure on any Kubernetes cluster. You will work within the foundational services layer to ensure our storage solutions are performant, scalable, and resilient.The Technical Surface  You will work across the AWC stack, contributing to:   Rust: Implementing high-performance components using async I/O with tokio and ensuring safe, reliable data handling. Go: Developing Kubernetes-native controllers and operators to manage lifecycle events, stateful sets, and resource orchestration. Kubernetes: Operating within complex cluster environments, utilizing features like mTLS (Istio), pod affinity, and custom resource definitions (CRDs). Distributed Systems: Contributing to logic for erasure coding, consensus protocols (e.g., Ratis), and data replication strategies.    What You'll Actually Do   Build & Ship: Take ownership of features from design specification to production validation, ensuring high code quality and test coverage. Collaborate: Partner with team members across Rust, Go, and Java to connect disparate layers of the stack. Quality Assurance: Participate in rigorous code reviews, focusing on invariant verification and clear failure mode articulation. Solve Problems: Engage in root cause analysis for distributed system defects, proposing and implementing long-term architectural solutions rather than temporary patches. Document: Create and maintain technical design specs, ensuring architectural decisions are clear for the rest of the engineering team.    What You Bring - Required   Experience: 5+ years of experience building production-grade distributed systems. You have owned systems through the full lifecycle, from design and implementation to on-call support. Languages: Strong expertise in at least one of Rust, Go, or Java. You are comfortable diving into a multi-language codebase and picking up new languages as needed. Systems Knowledge: Deep understanding of distributed systems principles (e.g., consensus, consistency models, latency vs. durability tradeoffs). Kubernetes Proficiency: Experience with Kubernetes internals, such as controllers, operators, or networking across CNI/Istio. Pragmatism: You balance the ""perfect"" architectural solution with the reality of shipping production software on time. You push back on unnecessary complexity.    Strongly Preferred   Storage Background: Experience with HDFS, S3, Apache Ozone, or similar object storage systems. Performance Engineering: Experience profiling and optimizing systems (e.g., using flamegraphs or allocator tuning) to improve throughput or latency. Open Source: A history of contributing to CNCF or Apache projects (e.g., kubebuilder, controller-runtime, RocksDB, tonic).    Bonus   Erasure Coding: Familiarity with ISA-L, Jerasure, or understanding how CPU vectorization impacts reconstruction throughput. Service Mesh: Experience debugging mTLS handshakes or optimizing L7 proxy configurations.
